tool.name: Batch Dispersion
tool.description: Indicators computation and convex hull plots to assess intra and inter batch dispersion.

param.name: dataMatrix
param.label: Data matrix file
param.help: Main data matrix. Rows are variables (features), columns are samples. The first column must contain variable identifiers, and the first row must contain sample identifiers.

param.name: sampleMetadata
param.label: Sample metadata file
param.help: Sample metadata table. Each row corresponds to a sample, and columns provide sample annotations (e.g., class, batch, group). The first column must contain sample identifiers matching the data matrix columns.

param.name: variableMetadata
param.label: Variable metadata file
param.help: Variable metadata table. Each row corresponds to a variable (feature), and columns provide variable annotations (e.g., m/z, retention time). The first column must contain variable identifiers matching the data matrix rows.

param.name: batch_col
param.label: The sampleMetadata column with batch information

param.name: sample_order_col
param.label: The sampleMetadata column with sample order information

param.name: variables
param.label: An optional subset of variables to analyse

param.name: mode
param.label: Sample order mode
param.help: Use the global sample order or a batch-wise one (affect inter-batch dispersion and ratio computations)

param.name: single_graph
param.label: Display all variables on the same graph (in case of global sample order)

*************************************** Batch Dispersion (Convex Hull Analysis) ***************************************
=========== DESCRIPTION ===========
This tool assesses variability from data obtained by a sequence of analysis involving multiple batches and analyses order, e.g. as in metabolomics which is the context of design of this tool. More precisely batch variability is assessed by plotting convex hulls around variable values (e.g. metabolites intensities) ordered by analysis order (e.g. injection order). It computes three dispersion indicators for each variable:
- **Intra Batch Convex Dispersion**: Variability within each batch - **Inter Batch Convex Dispersion**: Variability between batches - **Intra/Inter Batch Dispersion Ratio**: Ratio of intra-batch to inter-batch dispersion
These indicators help assess data quality and batch consistency, particularly for QC samples, pooled samples, or reference materials.
---------------------------------------------------
========================== ALIGNMENT WITH OTHER TOOLS ==========================
----------- INPUT FILES -----------
+----------------------------+---------+ | Parameter : num + label | Format | +============================+=========+ | 1 : Data matrix file | tabular | +----------------------------+---------+ | 2 : SampleMetadata file | tabular | +----------------------------+---------+ | 3 : VariableMetadata file | tabular | +----------------------------+---------+
**Data matrix file:** | Tabular file with variable abundance data. Rows represent variables, columns represent samples. | First column should contain variable identifiers.
**Sample metadata file:** | TSV file with sample information. Rows represent samples (must match Data matrix columns). | Must contain columns for batch information and injection/sample order.
**Variable metadata file:** | TSV file with variable information. Rows represent variables (must match Data matrix rows). | First column should contain variable identifiers. | Output will include three new columns with computed dispersion indicators.
.. class:: warningmark
For more information about input file formats, refer to the "W4M HowTo" page: | `W4M table format for Galaxy <https://nextcloud.inrae.fr/s/qLkNZRf84QQ5YLY>`_
------------ OUTPUT FILES ------------
**Convex Hull Plot (PDF):** | PDF file containing visualizations of convex hulls for all selected variables. | Each plot shows intensity values (y-axis) vs. injection order (x-axis), grouped by batch. | Data points may be displayed as individual markers.
**Variable Metadata Output (TSV):** | Updated variable metadata file with three new columns containing dispersion indicators for each variable: | | - IntraBatchConvexDispersion: Dispersion within each batch | - InterBatchConvexDispersion: Dispersion between batches | - IntraInterBatchDispersionRatio: Ratio of intra-batch to inter-batch dispersion
---------------------------------------------------
============================ EXAMPLE OF WORKFLOW POSITION ============================
- **Before batch correction:** Assess batch variability in raw data - **After batch correction:** Verify that batch correction has improved consistency - **During QC analysis:** Monitor consistency of QC or pool samples across runs
---------------------------------------------------
=============== TOOL PARAMETERS ===============
**batch_col:** | Column name or index in Sample metadata containing batch identifiers. | Used to group samples by batch for dispersion analysis.
**sample_order_col:** | Column name or index in Sample metadata containing analysis/sample order information (e.g., injectionOrder). | Used to define the order for plotting convex hulls.
**variables (optional):** | Select specific variables to analyze. If empty, all variables from the variable metadata are analyzed. | Multiple variables can be selected.
**mode:** | **"batchwise":** Performs batchwise analysis within each batch separately. | **"global" (default):** Uses global sample order across all batches for convex analysis.
**single_graph:** | **TRUE (checked):** Display all variables on the same graph (in case of global sample order). | **FALSE (unchecked):** Display each variable on a separate graph. | Default: FALSE
**points:** | **TRUE (checked):** Display individual intensity data points on the convex hull plots. | **FALSE (unchecked):** Show only the convex hull polygon without data points. | Default: TRUE
---------------------------------------------------
============== EXAMPLE OF USE ==============
**Typical workflow in metabolomics:**
1. Run MS data extraction (e.g., XCMS, CAMERA) 2. Select Data matrix, Sample metadata, and Variable metadata outputs 3. Select the batch column (e.g., "batch") 4. Select the injection order column (e.g., "injectionOrder") 5. Optionally select specific metabolites to visualize 6. Set "Global Mode" based on your analysis needs 7. Run the tool 8. Examine the PDF plots to visually assess batch consistency 9. Use the output variable metadata with dispersion indicators for further analysis
**Interpreting Results:**
- Low IntraBatchConvexDispersion or InterBatchConvexDispersion reflect low intra or inter batch dispersion - Low IntraInterBatchDispersionRatio (between 0 and 1) suggests potential batch effects or drift - Compare dispersion indicators across different metabolites to identify problematic ions
---------------------------------------------------
------------ KNOWN ISSUES ------------
- Missing or zero intensity values are imputed using median value before convex analysis
